signin.availability: Always shown. It works only for an account that already exists. Type your email address, then type the code we send you.
Only if your browser supports passkeys. A "Use a passkey" button then appears. It works only with a passkey you already have for this site. You cannot add a passkey on the site yet.
Only on a site that has the forum connection switched on. A "Continue with rapamycin.news" button then appears.

steps.action: Read what biohack.it is for. From here you can start, sign in, open the ecosystem page or open the documentation.

Choose "Get started". Sign-up and sign-in are the same page. An email code does not create a new account. A new account is created today only when you continue with the forum button, on a site that has it switched on.
Choose "Sign in" and pick one of the sign-in methods below.

If you start from "Get started" and sign in with an email code or a passkey, a welcome page opens. It explains that your profile is public by default. If you sign in with a provider button, you go to the dashboard address instead.
The ecosystem page lists the open projects and open data that biohack.it reuses.

Open "Import lab results (CSV)" on the home page after you sign in. Choose a file and press "Check file". Each row is marked Recognised or Not recognised, with the reason. "Save report" works only when every row is recognised. After saving you can press "Undo this import".
steps.step: Import lab results from a CSV file

steps.action: Open "Enter lab results by hand" (a link on the import page, or /labs/new) after you sign in. For each result type the LOINC code, the value exactly as your lab printed it, and the unit. Laboratory, method, device and dates are optional. Use "Add another result" for more rows. "Save report" opens the saved report. If a value is refused, the reason is shown next to that result and field, and nothing you typed is cleared.
steps.step: Type a lab report by hand

steps.action: Open a saved report (the link after saving, or /labs/reports/<number>). Each result shows the value and unit as reported, laboratory, method, device and dates, its validation state, whether it is counted in aggregations, and a range check in words. Below the table, each result is shown against its three ranges, kept separate: the laboratory reference range, the longevity-optimal range and the safety threshold, each with its status in words and its source (shown by frontend/src/components/ResultRanges.tsx). "About this optimal range" opens the source, population, endpoint, evidence grade and last-reviewed date. A typed result looks the same as an imported one. "Undo this report" appears only for imported reports and deletes the report after you confirm; a report you typed by hand cannot be undone.
The documentation index links to the AI surfaces map, the architecture page and this guide.
